problems.title: Implement a Shuffle Buffer for Streaming Data
problems.description: Build a shuffle buffer that wraps an IterableDataset, providing approximate shuffling with O(buffer_size) memory.
problems.question: v3/data-loading/buffered-loading/buffered-loading.ipynb
hints: Pull buffer_size items from iter(base_dataset) into a list first; when the stream runs dry before that, you simply start with a smaller buffer.
Then, for every further item from the stream: pick a uniformly random slot, yield what is in it, and put the new item in that slot.
When the stream is exhausted, the buffer still holds up to buffer_size items: random.shuffle it and yield them all — otherwise they are lost.

problems.title: Simulate DistributedSampler for Data Parallel Training
problems.description: Implement a distributed sampler from scratch that shards a dataset across ranks with deterministic shuffling and padding.
problems.question: v3/data-loading/data-parallel-loading/data-parallel-loading.ipynb
hints: Every rank gets num_samples = ceil(len(dataset) / num_replicas) indices, so the padded index list has total_size = num_samples * num_replicas entries.
In __iter__, build one index list that is identical on every rank: torch.randperm(n, generator=g) with g.manual_seed(seed + epoch) when shuffling, else range(n) — never seed with the rank.
Pad by appending indices from the start (repeat the list if padding > n), then take indices[rank::num_replicas] as this rank's shard.

problems.title: Implement a Preloaded Map-Style Dataset
problems.description: Build a map-style Dataset that loads all data into memory and integrates with DataLoader for batching and shuffling.
problems.question: v3/data-loading/preloaded-dataset/preloaded-dataset.ipynb
hints: A map-style dataset needs exactly two methods besides __init__: __len__ (how many samples) and __getitem__(idx) (one sample). DataLoader does the batching and shuffling by calling them.
Convert once, in __init__: torch.as_tensor accepts tensors, numpy arrays and lists. Check that X and y have the same number of samples there, and raise if they do not.
__len__ is the number of rows of X (its first dimension, not the feature count); __getitem__ returns the tuple (self.X[idx], self.y[idx]) — no dict, no batching inside the dataset.

problems.title: Implement a Streaming IterableDataset with Yield
problems.description: Build an IterableDataset that streams data line by line from a file using a generator, with multi-worker sharding support.
problems.question: v3/data-loading/streaming-dataset/streaming-dataset.ipynb
hints: Open the file inside __iter__ and loop over it — a Python file object is a lazy line iterator. Parse each line into x (all but the last value) and a scalar y (the last one) and yield them.
Every DataLoader worker runs its own copy of __iter__. torch.utils.data.get_worker_info() is None in the main process; inside a worker it has .id and .num_workers.
Shard by line number: enumerate the lines and keep only those with line_idx % num_workers == worker_id, treating the main process as worker 0 of 1.

__getitem__(i) returns the pair (X[i], y[i]) — DataLoader stacks those into batches for you, so do not batch inside the Dataset.

forward(x) is custom_activation(self.linear(x)) — the activation goes on the output of the single linear layer.

hints: Huber is quadratic for small errors and linear for large ones.
The switch happens at |error| == delta.
0.5*e^2 below the threshold; delta*(|e| - 0.5*delta) above it.

problems.question: torch/basic/save-model/save_model.ipynb
hints: Everything here is torch.save / torch.load plus the state_dict methods. A state dict maps names to tensors — parameters and buffers such as BatchNorm's running statistics — so it loads without your class's code being pickled.

load_for_inference builds a fresh model with model_class(), loads the file with torch.load(path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=True), calls load_state_dict and then eval() — Dropout and BatchNorm behave differently in training mode.

A checkpoint is one dict with the keys 'epoch', 'model_state_dict' and 'optimizer_state_dict'. load_checkpoint calls load_state_dict on the model and on the optimizer it was given (not a new one) and returns checkpoint['epoch'] — without the optimizer state, momentum and Adam's moments restart from zero.

problems.title: Implement a CNN on CIFAR-10
problems.description: Build and train a convolutional neural network to classify CIFAR-10 images using conv layers, pooling, and batch norm.
problems.question: torch/easy/cnn/CNN.ipynb
hints: CIFAR-10 images are 3x32x32 and there are 10 classes.
Track the spatial size through each pool: 32 -> 16 after one 2x2 pool.
The first Linear needs in_features = channels * height * width after flattening.

problems.title: Implement an RNN from Scratch
problems.description: Write a recurrent neural network cell from scratch using raw tensor operations, implementing the hidden state update manually.
problems.question: torch/easy/rnn/RNN.ipynb
hints: Keep a hidden state h of shape (batch, hidden_dim), start it at zeros on every forward call, and update it once per timestep in a Python loop over seq_len.
The update is h = tanh(x_t W_ih + h W_hh + b) with the same W_ih, W_hh and b at every step (store them as nn.Parameter); x_t is x[:, t] because the input is (batch, seq_len, input_dim).
After the loop, the final h summarises the whole sequence: map it with nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1) to get one prediction per sequence, shape (batch, 1).

problems.title: Data Augmentation with torchvision.transforms
problems.description: Build CIFAR-10 train and test pipelines with torchvision.transforms: random flips, padded random crops and per-channel normalization for training, and a deterministic pipeline for evaluation.
problems.question: torch/easy/augmentation/augmentation.ipynb
hints: Both pipelines are a transforms.Compose list. The test pipeline only converts and normalises; the training pipeline adds the random augmentations in front.

PIL-space operations (RandomHorizontalFlip, RandomCrop) go before ToTensor, and Normalize goes last because it needs a tensor. The pad value of the crop is then a black pixel, as in the original images' borders.

Training: RandomHorizontalFlip(p=0.5), RandomCrop(32, padding=4), ToTensor(), Normalize(CIFAR10_MEAN, CIFAR10_STD). Test: ToTensor() and the same Normalize only — no random transform, so evaluation is deterministic.

problems.title: Add Benchmarking to PyTorch Code
problems.description: Time a training loop correctly (perf_counter, CUDA synchronization, warm-up) and micro-benchmark a forward pass with torch.utils.benchmark, comparing autograd against inference_mode.
problems.question: torch/easy/benchmark/bench.ipynb
hints: Flatten the 28x28 image (x.flatten(1)) and stack at least two hidden nn.Linear layers with a ReLU after each, ending in a Linear to 10 logits.
Time with time.perf_counter(), not time.time(), and expect the first epoch to be slower: it pays one-off warm-up costs.

CUDA kernels launch asynchronously: call torch.cuda.synchronize() before starting and before stopping the clock. torch.utils.benchmark.Timer does the warm-up, synchronization and repetition for you (but defaults to num_threads=1).

problems.title: Train an Autoencoder for Anomaly Detection
problems.description: Build an autoencoder that learns normal data patterns, then detect anomalies by measuring reconstruction error.
problems.question: torch/easy/autoencoder/autoencoder.ipynb
hints: Without a bottleneck an autoencoder can learn the identity and reconstruct anomalies as well as normal digits — compress each 784-pixel image to a code much smaller than that (e.g. conv/pool down to 7x7, then a Linear to 32 numbers).

Mirror the encoder: Linear back to the 7x7 feature map, then ConvTranspose2d(kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1) twice (7 -> 14 -> 28) and a Sigmoid, because the pixels are in [0, 1].

Score every image separately — average the squared error over C, H and W but not over the batch, so 64 images give 64 scores. Set the threshold to a high percentile (e.g. the 95th) of the scores on held-out normal images, never on test labels.

problems.title: Quantize Your Language Model
problems.description: Apply post-training quantization to reduce model size and inference latency while maintaining accuracy.
problems.question: torch/easy/quantize-lm/quantize-language-model.ipynb
hints: LanguageModel(vocab_size, embed_size, hidden_size, num_layers): Embedding -> LSTM(batch_first=True) -> Linear -> Softmax.
Predict the *next* token, so take the last timestep of the LSTM output (lstm_out[:, -1, :]) before the Linear — the result is (batch, vocab_size).
torch.ao.quantization.quantize_dynamic(model, {nn.Linear, nn.LSTM}, dtype=torch.qint8) only rewrites modules it recognises, so build the model out of nn.Linear / nn.LSTM rather than raw matmuls.

problems.title: Mixed Precision Training with torch.amp
problems.description: Use automatic mixed precision (torch.autocast + torch.amp.GradScaler) to train in float16/bfloat16, with loss scaling against float16 gradient underflow and skipped steps on overflow.
problems.question: torch/easy/cuda-amp/cuda-amp.ipynb
hints: float16 has a narrow exponent range: small gradients underflow to zero, so it needs loss scaling (an enabled GradScaler). bfloat16 has float32's range and needs none — return a GradScaler built with enabled=False so train_step can call it the same way on both paths.

Only the forward pass and the loss go inside torch.autocast(device_type=inputs.device.type, dtype=amp_dtype); backward runs outside it. Zero the gradients every step, and never cast the model itself to half precision.

Order matters: backward through the scaled loss, unscale the optimizer's gradients, clip them to max_norm=1.0, step through the scaler, then update the scale. Clipping before unscaling clips the scaled gradients (S times too big), and stepping the optimizer directly applies inf/NaN updates after an overflow that the scaler would have skipped.

problems.title: CNN Parameter Initialization
problems.description: Explore how different weight initialization strategies (Xavier, Kaiming, etc.) affect CNN training convergence.
problems.question: torch/medium/cnn-param-init/CNN_ParamInit.ipynb
hints: config_init returns the initializer *function*, it does not run it — you use it as `model.apply(config_init('xavier'))`.
Each initializer takes one module and should only touch it when it is an nn.Conv2d or nn.Linear; apply() walks containers and activations too.
torch.nn.init has all four: zeros_, normal_, xavier_normal_ (variance 2/(fan_in + fan_out)) and kaiming_normal_ with nonlinearity='relu' (variance 2/fan_in). Do not forget the bias.

problems.title: Implement a CNN from Scratch
problems.description: Build convolutional layers from raw tensor operations — implementing forward passes with cross-correlation and learnable filters.
problems.question: torch/medium/cnn-scratch/CNN_scratch.ipynb
hints: Output size is (H + 2*padding - kernel) // stride + 1 per spatial dim.
F.unfold turns sliding windows into columns if you want to avoid Python loops.
Do not forget to add the bias, once per output channel.

problems.title: Implement an LSTM from Scratch
problems.description: Code the LSTM cell equations from scratch: forget gate, input gate, cell state update, and output gate using raw tensors.
problems.question: torch/medium/lstm/LSTM.ipynb
hints: CustomLSTMModel(input_dim, hidden_units).forward(inputs, H_C=None) returns (predictions, (H, C)) with predictions shaped (batch, seq_len, 1).
Per timestep: i, f, o = sigmoid(...), C~ = tanh(...), C = f*C + i*C~, H = o*tanh(C). Stack every H and push the stack through the Linear.
When H_C is given, start from it instead of a fresh state — that is what makes the model resumable, and zeros (not randn) are the right default.

problems.title: Implement AlexNet from Scratch
problems.description: Recreate the AlexNet architecture that started the deep learning revolution, with its 5 conv + 3 FC layer design.
problems.question: torch/medium/alexnet/alexnet.ipynb
hints: AlexNet expects 3x224x224 input and ends in a classifier over num_classes.
Five conv layers with max-pooling, then three fully connected layers.

Track the spatial size through each stride and pool to size the first Linear: with an 11x11 / stride-4 / padding-2 first conv and three 3x3 / stride-2 max-pools, 224 -> 55 -> 27 -> 13 -> 6, so the first Linear takes 256*6*6.

problems.title: Train a 3D CNN for CT Image Segmentation
problems.description: Extend 2D convolutions to 3D for volumetric medical image segmentation on CT scans.
problems.question: torch/medium/3dcnn/3DCNN.ipynb
hints: The input is [B, D, C, W, H]. Fold depth into the batch (view(B*D, C, W, H)) for the 2D backbone, then unfold and permute to [B, C, D, W, H] for Conv3d — and permute back to [B, D, 1, W, H] at the end so pred lines up with the masks.
ResNet-18 with its last two children stripped divides W and H by 32, so the ConvTranspose3d stack has to multiply them back by 32 — use kernel/stride (1, k, k) so the depth axis is left alone.
Dice over binary masks is 2*|pred ∩ label| / (|pred| + |label|); finish the network with sigmoid so pred is a probability the overlap can be computed on.

problems.title: Write a Custom Autograd Function (SILU)
problems.description: Implement SiLU activation with a custom autograd Function, defining both forward and backward passes manually.
problems.question: torch/hard/custom-autograd/custom-autgrad-function.ipynb
hints: forward(ctx, x, slope) returns slope * x * sigmoid(x); stash what backward needs with ctx.save_for_backward(x, slope), not as attributes on ctx.
d/dx [x*sigmoid(x)] = sigmoid(x) + x*sigmoid(x)*(1 - sigmoid(x)); multiply by slope and by grad_output.

backward must return one gradient per forward input: d/dslope is grad_output * x * sigmoid(x), summed back down to slope's shape (slope was broadcast over x). Keep the slope an nn.Parameter in the model so the optimizer updates it.

problems.title: Write a Transformer from Scratch
problems.description: Build a Transformer encoder classifier from scratch — sinusoidal positional encoding, multi-head self-attention with a padding mask, position-wise feed-forward and pre-LN residual blocks, read out from a CLS token.
problems.question: torch/hard/transformer/transformer.ipynb
hints: Shapes: everything below the model works on (batch, seq_len, embed_dim) and returns the same shape.
In attention, split the last dim into (num_heads, head_dim) and move heads next to the batch: (B, H, T, head_dim). Scale the scores by 1/sqrt(head_dim) before the softmax over the *last* axis.
PositionalEncoding builds a (max_len, d_model) table once with sin(pos/10000^(2i/d)) and cos(...), registers it as a buffer, and forward just adds the first seq_len rows to x.

Padding: key_padding_mask is (B, T) bool with True at pad positions. Fill those *key* columns of the (B, H, T, T) scores with -inf before the softmax (mask[:, None, None, :]). In the model, prepend one False column for the CLS token before passing the mask to every layer.

problems.title: Write a GAN
problems.description: Implement a generative adversarial network: competing generator and discriminator networks trained adversarially with binary cross-entropy and the non-saturating generator loss.
problems.question: torch/hard/GAN/GAN.ipynb
hints: Generator(input_dim, output_dim) maps a latent vector to one fake sample; Discriminator(input_dim) maps a sample to a single number.
End the generator with Tanh so samples live in [-1, 1], and the discriminator with Sigmoid so its output is a probability BCELoss can take.
When you train the generator do NOT detach the fake batch — the gradient has to flow back through the discriminator into the generator.

Training loop: D step = BCE(D(real), 1) + BCE(D(G(z).detach()), 0); G step = BCE(D(G(z)), 1) on a fake batch that is NOT detached (fresh noise, or the same G(z) the D step detached) — the non-saturating -log D(G(z)), not log(1 - D(G(z))). zero_grad the optimizer you are about to step before its backward().

problems.title: Sequence-to-Sequence with Attention
problems.description: Build an encoder-decoder model with Bahdanau attention for sequence transduction tasks like translation.
problems.question: torch/hard/seq-seq/seq-to-seq-with-Attention.ipynb
hints: Encoder(input_dim, embed_dim, hidden_dim, num_layers): nn.Embedding over the source vocabulary, then nn.LSTM(embed_dim, hidden_dim, num_layers, batch_first=True).
forward returns (outputs, (hidden, cell)) — the attention needs every timestep, the decoder needs the final states to start from.
With batch_first=True outputs is (batch, src_len, hidden_dim) while hidden and cell stay (num_layers, batch, hidden_dim).

Decoder attention (Bahdanau): score every encoder output h_i against the decoder's top-layer state s = hidden[-1] with e_i = v^T tanh(W_s s + W_h h_i), giving (batch, src_len) scores; softmax over the source axis. Nothing in the decoder may assume a fixed source length.

context = torch.bmm(weights.unsqueeze(1), encoder_outputs) is (batch, 1, hidden_dim). Concatenate it with the embedded token, project back to embed_dim with tanh, run ONE LSTM step from (hidden, cell), and map the LSTM output to vocabulary logits.

problems.title: Explainable AI with Grad-CAM
problems.description: Visualize which image regions drive a CNN's prediction with Grad-CAM: hooks capture a late layer's activations and gradients, and gradient-weighted feature maps give the heatmap.
problems.question: torch/hard/xai/xai.ipynb
hints: You need two tensors from the target layer: its output A (forward) and the gradient of the class score with respect to A (backward). A forward hook on target_layer can keep A; from there A.register_hook or torch.autograd.grad gives dy^c/dA. Keep the handle that register_forward_hook returns so you can remove the hook again.

Score each sample by the logit of its own class (gather along dim 1, never the softmax) and sum those scores, so one backward pass gives every sample its own gradient. alpha is that gradient averaged over the spatial dims (2, 3) only — not over the batch — and the map is ReLU of the alpha-weighted sum of A over the channel dim: shape (N, h, w), not normalised.

For a frozen model inside torch.no_grad(): run the forward under torch.enable_grad() on a detached copy of x that requires grad, so a graph exists without touching the parameters. Remove the hook in a finally block. upsample_cam: F.interpolate on cam.unsqueeze(1) with mode='bilinear', align_corners=False, then divide each map by its own amax over (H, W) plus a small eps such as 1e-8.

problems.title: Implement Adam from Scratch
problems.description: Implement the Adam optimizer from scratch on top of torch.optim.Optimizer: exponential moving averages of the gradient and its square, with bias correction.
problems.question: torch/hard/optimizers/adam/adam.ipynb
hints: Subclass torch.optim.Optimizer and keep per-parameter state in self.state[p] — it starts as an empty dict, so initialize it on the first step. Do the whole update under @torch.no_grad() with in-place ops (mul_, add_, addcmul_, addcdiv_).
Adam: m = b1*m + (1-b1)*g and v = b2*v + (1-b2)*g^2, then correct both by (1 - beta**step) and update p -= lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps).

problems.title: Implement AdamW from Scratch
problems.description: Implement the AdamW optimizer from scratch on top of torch.optim.Optimizer: Adam's update with weight decay decoupled from the gradient, applied directly to the parameters.
problems.question: torch/hard/optimizers/adamw/adamw.ipynb
hints: Subclass torch.optim.Optimizer and keep per-parameter state in self.state[p] — it starts as an empty dict, so initialize it on the first step. Do the whole update under @torch.no_grad() with in-place ops (mul_, add_, addcmul_, addcdiv_).

AdamW: m = b1*m + (1-b1)*g and v = b2*v + (1-b2)*g^2, then correct both by (1 - beta**step) and update p -= lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps). Weight decay is p.mul_(1 - lr * weight_decay) applied directly to the parameter — do NOT add weight_decay * p to the gradient, that is L2 regularization and the adaptive denominator rescales it.

problems.title: Implement Muon from Scratch
problems.description: Implement the Muon optimizer from scratch on top of torch.optim.Optimizer: momentum orthogonalized by Newton–Schulz for matrix parameters, with an AdamW fallback for 1D parameters.
problems.question: torch/hard/optimizers/muon/muon.ipynb
hints: Subclass torch.optim.Optimizer and keep per-parameter state in self.state[p] — it starts as an empty dict, so initialize it on the first step. Do the whole update under @torch.no_grad() with in-place ops (mul_, add_, addcmul_, addcdiv_).

newton_schulz: transpose a tall X so X @ X.T is the small Gram matrix, divide by the Frobenius norm (+ eps) so every singular value is <= 1, then repeat A = X @ X.T; X = a*X + (b*A + c*A@A) @ X with Muon's (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315). The singular values end up in about [0.7, 1.2] — that is expected, not a bug.

Muon on a matrix: buf = momentum*buf + grad, update = grad + momentum*buf (Nesterov) or buf; flatten it to (len(p), -1), orthogonalize with newton_schulz, scale by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)), decay p by (1 - lr*weight_decay), then p -= lr * scale * update reshaped to p.shape. Only ndim >= 2 — 1D params get the AdamW fallback.

problems.title: Create Embeddings out of an LLM
problems.description: Turn a causal LM's (SmolLM2-135M) final hidden states into sentence embeddings with masked mean pooling or last-token pooling, and rank reviews by cosine similarity to a keyword.
problems.question: llm/Create-Embeddings-out-of-an-LLM/embeddings-q2.ipynb
hints: Both poolings must ignore padding, and attention_mask (1 = real token, 0 = padding) says where it is. Turn it into a float of shape (batch, seq_len, 1) so it broadcasts against the (batch, seq_len, hidden) states.

Mean pooling: zero the padded states, sum over the sequence dim, and divide by each row's number of real tokens (the mask summed over seq_len, clamped to at least 1) — not by seq_len. Last-token pooling: find one position per row, then index hidden_states[arange(batch), positions].

The last real token sits at the last index where the mask is 1. With right padding that is (number of real tokens - 1); with left padding it is always seq_len - 1. seq_len - 1 minus the position of the first 1 in the mask flipped along seq_len covers both (argmax returns the first maximum).

problems.title: Flash Attention
problems.description: Implement the FlashAttention forward pass — tiled attention with an online softmax (running max, running denominator, rescaled accumulator) and the logsumexp output — in PyTorch, then as a Triton kernel.
problems.question: llm/Flash-Attention/flash-attention.ipynb
hints: Walk K/V in tiles and never build the full score matrix. Per query row keep a running max m, a running softmax denominator l and an unnormalized output accumulator, starting from -inf, 0 and 0.
When a tile raises the max to m_new, rescale l and the accumulator by alpha = exp(m - m_new) before adding the tile: l = alpha*l + p.sum(-1), acc = alpha*acc + p @ V_tile, with p = exp(s - m_new).
Divide the accumulator by l only once, after the last tile. L is the logsumexp of the scaled scores: m + log(l) at the end.

problems.title: Implement RMS Norm
problems.description: Build Root Mean Square Layer Normalization used in LLaMA and modern transformers — simpler and faster than LayerNorm.
problems.question: llm/RMS-Norm/rms-norm.ipynb
hints: Square the input, take the mean along the last dimension, add epsilon, then take the square root.
Use keepdim=True in the mean so broadcasting works when you divide.
The scale parameter gamma should have shape (dim,) and be created with nn.Parameter(torch.ones(dim)).

problems.title: Implement Byte Pair Encoding from Scratch
problems.description: Build the BPE tokenizer algorithm that iteratively merges frequent character pairs to build a subword vocabulary.
problems.question: llm/Byte-Pair-Encoder/BPE-q3.ipynb
hints: get_vocab splits each word into characters plus an end-of-word marker, and counts it.
get_stats counts adjacent symbol pairs weighted by each word's frequency.
A merge replaces every adjacent (a, b) with the single symbol 'ab' — the spelling of each word must not change, only how it is chopped up.

problems.title: Implement Attention from Scratch
problems.description: Build scaled dot-product attention from raw matrix operations — queries, keys, values, scaling, and softmax.
problems.question: llm/Implement-Attention-from-Scratch/attention-q4-Question.ipynb
hints: scores = q @ k.transpose(-2,-1) / sqrt(d_k), then softmax, then @ v.
Divide by sqrt(d_k) or the softmax saturates as dimension grows.
Masked positions become -inf BEFORE the softmax, not zero after it.

problems.title: Implement Multi-Head Attention from Scratch
problems.description: Split attention into multiple heads with independent projections, compute attention per head, and concatenate results.
problems.question: llm/Multi-Head-Attention/multi-head-attention-q5-Question.ipynb
hints: Project q, k and v with their weights (x @ W.T), split d_model into num_heads chunks of d_head = d_model // num_heads, attend within each head, then merge the heads and apply W_o.
Reshape (batch, seq, d_model) to (batch, num_heads, seq, d_head) with view + transpose(1, 2), and scale the scores by 1/sqrt(d_head), not 1/sqrt(d_model).
After softmax(scores) @ V, undo the split with transpose(1, 2) and .contiguous().view(batch, seq_q, d_model) before W_o. Positions where the mask is False get -inf before the softmax.

problems.title: Implement Grouped Query Attention from Scratch
problems.description: Build GQA where multiple query heads share key-value heads, reducing KV cache memory while preserving quality.
problems.question: llm/Grouped-Query-Attention/grouped-query-attention-Question.ipynb
hints: Queries keep all num_query_heads heads; keys and values only have num_query_groups heads, each shared by a group of g = num_query_heads // num_query_groups query heads.
W_k and W_v project to num_query_groups * d_head features, not d_model — that is where the KV-cache saving comes from. Split them into num_query_groups heads.
Expand K/V with repeat_interleave(g, dim=1) so query head h uses K/V head h // g (a plain repeat/tile would pair it with h % num_query_groups), then attend as in MHA.

problems.title: Implement Sinusoidal Embeddings
problems.description: Build the fixed sinusoidal positional encoding from 'Attention Is All You Need' using sin/cos at different frequencies.
problems.question: llm/Sinusoidal-Positional-Embedding/sinusoidal-q7-Question.ipynb
hints: Even dimensions 2i get sin and odd dimensions 2i+1 get cos. The pair shares one frequency.
i is 0, 1, ..., d_model/2 - 1, not the raw dimension. The frequency is 1 / 10000**(2i/d_model).
It is a fixed function of position — register it as a buffer, not a parameter.

problems.title: Implement RoPE Embeddings
problems.description: Build Rotary Position Embeddings that encode relative positions by rotating query and key vectors in complex space.
problems.question: llm/Rotary-Positional-Embedding/rope-q8-Question.ipynb
hints: RoPE turns each pair of features by an angle m * theta_i (position times a per-pair frequency). A rotation keeps norms, and q_m . k_n then depends only on m - n.
Write the 2D rotation elementwise: x*cos + rotate_half(x)*sin, where rotate_half maps each pair (a, b) to (-b, a). Rotate q and k the same way.
Half-split convention: rotate_half returns cat(-x2, x1) of the two halves, and cos/sin repeat the angles as cat(freqs, freqs); they broadcast against (batch, heads, seq, head_dim).

problems.title: Implement SmolLM from Scratch
problems.description: Build SmolLM-135M (Llama architecture: RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, tied embeddings) from scratch, load the pretrained weights and match the reference logits.
problems.question: llm/SmolLM/smollm-q12-Question.ipynb
hints: rotate_half splits the last dim in half and returns (-x2, x1) concatenated.
repeat_kv expands each KV head n_rep times *in place* so head i of Q pairs with KV head i // n_rep — expand + reshape, not a plain repeat/tile.
RopeAttention: project, split into num_heads (Q) and kv_heads (K/V), rotate Q and K, repeat_kv the K/V, then scaled dot-product attention plus the additive mask.

problems.title: Implement Softmax from Scratch
problems.description: Build numerically stable softmax from raw tensor ops by subtracting the max along dim (the same shift behind the log-sum-exp trick), so exp() never overflows.
problems.question: v3/classical-ml/softmax/softmax.ipynb
hints: exp() of a large number overflows. What can you subtract without changing the result?
softmax(x) == softmax(x - c) for any constant c. Pick c = max(x) along `dim`.
Keep dims when you take the max and the sum so broadcasting lines up.

problems.title: Implement K-Means Clustering in PyTorch
problems.description: Code Lloyd's algorithm with PyTorch tensors: random init, distance computation, centroid updates, and convergence check.
problems.question: v3/classical-ml/kmeans/kmeans.ipynb
hints: Alternate two steps: assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to the mean of its points.
torch.cdist(data, centroids) gives you all the distances at once.
Stop when the centroids stop moving by more than `tol`.

problems.title: Implement KNN in PyTorch
problems.description: Build k-nearest neighbors classification using vectorized distance computation and top-k selection on tensors.
problems.question: v3/classical-ml/knn/knn.ipynb
hints: torch.cdist gives every test-to-train distance in one call.
topk(..., largest=False) picks the nearest neighbours.
Predict the majority label among those neighbours (torch.mode helps).

problems.title: Implement Logistic Regression with Gradient Descent
problems.description: Build binary logistic regression from scratch with sigmoid, binary cross-entropy, and manual gradient descent updates.
problems.question: v3/classical-ml/logistic-regression/logistic-regression.ipynb
hints: sigmoid(z) = 1 / (1 + exp(-z)).
BCE = -mean(y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)); clamp p away from 0 and 1 first.
Train with gradient descent on the BCE of sigmoid(Xw + b).

problems.title: Implement Contrastive Loss (InfoNCE) + CLIP Training Loop
problems.description: Build the InfoNCE contrastive loss and a CLIP-style training loop that aligns image and text embeddings.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/contrastive-loss-clip/contrastive-loss-clip.ipynb
hints: L2-normalize both feature sets first (F.normalize(x, dim=-1)); the cosine similarity matrix is then just image_features @ text_features.T.
The positives sit on the diagonal, so the cross-entropy targets are torch.arange(batch_size) — image i must match text i.

Symmetric means both directions: (cross_entropy(logits, labels) + cross_entropy(logits.T, labels)) / 2, with logits = cosine similarity * exp(log_temperature). That multiplier is CLIP's logit scale 1/tau (initialized to 1/0.07, clamped at 100); keep it learnable in log space.

problems.title: Implement 2D Positional Embeddings
problems.description: Build 2D sinusoidal position encodings for vision transformers, encoding both row and column positions in patch grids.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/2d-positional-embeddings/2d-positional-embeddings.ipynb
hints: Encode the row and the column separately, then concatenate the two halves.
Each half is a standard 1D sinusoidal embedding of size d_half = d_model // 2, with frequencies 1 / 10000^(2i / d_half) — so d_model must be divisible by 4.
Flatten the grid in row-major order so index r*width + c is position (r, c).

problems.title: Implement Top-p (Nucleus) Sampling
problems.description: Sort logits, compute cumulative probabilities, mask tokens below the nucleus threshold, and sample from the filtered distribution.
problems.question: v3/llm-decoding/top-p-sampling/top-p-sampling.ipynb
hints: Sort probabilities descending, then take the smallest prefix whose cumulative mass >= p — the token that crosses p is IN the nucleus.
Always keep at least the top token, renormalize the survivors, and map the sampled position back through the sort indices.
Drop a token when the mass ranked ABOVE it already reaches p: mask (cumsum - prob) >= p, i.e. the cumsum shifted right by one.

problems.title: Implement Top-k Sampling
problems.description: Select the k highest-probability tokens, zero out the rest, renormalize, and sample for controlled text generation.
problems.question: v3/llm-decoding/top-k-sampling/top-k-sampling.ipynb
hints: Keep the k largest logits and make the rest impossible to select.
Setting the discarded logits to -inf before the softmax does that cleanly.
torch.topk gives you both the values and their indices. Clamp k to the vocabulary size first — torch.topk raises if k > vocab_size.

problems.title: Implement Beam Search for LLM Decoding
problems.description: Maintain and expand top-scoring partial sequences at each decoding step with length normalization and early stopping.
problems.question: v3/llm-decoding/beam-search/beam-search.ipynb
hints: Keep each beam as (sequence, cumulative_log_prob) and start from ([start_token], 0.0) — the start token counts towards max_len.
Score a candidate with the RUNNING total: score + log_softmax(logits)[token]. Comparing only the current step's log-prob turns beam search into greedy.

Pool the candidates from every beam into one ranking (or flatten a (beams, vocab) score matrix and topk it), keep the top beam_width. A candidate ending in eos_token is finished: set it aside, never extend it.
At the end rank finished hypotheses and the beams still alive at max_len by score / num_generated ** length_penalty and return the best sequence.

problems.title: Implement Temperature Sampling
problems.description: Divide logits by a temperature scalar before softmax to sharpen or flatten the token probability distribution.
problems.question: v3/llm-decoding/temperature-sampling/temperature-sampling.ipynb
hints: Divide the logits by the temperature before the softmax.
Low temperature sharpens the distribution toward the argmax; high flattens it. temperature == 0 is the limit of that: return the argmax instead of dividing by zero.
Sample with torch.multinomial on the resulting probabilities.

problems.title: Implement LoRA on a Linear Layer
problems.description: Inject trainable low-rank decomposition matrices (A, B) into a frozen linear layer for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
problems.question: v3/alignment-training/lora/lora.ipynb
hints: LoRA adds a low-rank detour next to the frozen layer: output = linear(x) + (alpha/r) * (x @ A) @ B.
A is (d_in, rank) and B is (rank, d_out). Start B at zero and A random (bound ~1/sqrt(d_in)): the adapter is a no-op at step 0 but still gets a gradient.
Merging means W_new = W_old + (alpha/r) * (A @ B).T — the transpose matches nn.Linear's (d_out, d_in) weight layout.

problems.title: Implement KV Cache for Autoregressive Generation
problems.description: Cache key and value tensors from previous timesteps so each new token only computes attention over one new position.
problems.question: v3/llm-inference/kv-cache/kv-cache.ipynb
hints: The cache holds (batch, heads, seq_len, d_head). What changes as you decode?
update() appends the new K/V along the seq_len dimension (dim=2).

In cached mode you compute Q/K/V for the new token(s) only, then attend over the full cached K/V. A single decode token needs no causal mask (the cache only holds the past); a multi-token prefill chunk does, offset by the cached length.

problems.title: Implement Sliding Window Attention
problems.description: Restrict attention to a local window around each token (bidirectional or Mistral-style causal), cutting attention cost from O(n²) to O(n·w) for long sequences.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/sliding-window-attention/sliding-window-attention.ipynb
hints: Position i may attend to j when |i - j| <= window_size; with causal=True, only when also j <= i.

Build the mask from pairwise offsets: pos = torch.arange(seq_len), then (pos[:, None] - pos[None, :]).abs() <= window_size (rows are queries, columns keys). For causal=True, AND it with pos[:, None] >= pos[None, :].
Masked positions get -inf BEFORE the softmax, not zero after it, and the scores are scaled by 1/sqrt(d) as in ordinary attention.

problems.title: Implement DPO Loss from Scratch
problems.description: Compute the Direct Preference Optimization loss that trains a policy directly from preference pairs without a reward model.
problems.question: v3/alignment-training/dpo/dpo.ipynb
hints: get_batch_logps sums the log-probability of each actual next token, counting only the positions where loss_mask is 1 (the response, not the prompt or padding).
Shift by one: logits at position t predict the token at position t+1, so pair logits[:, :-1] with input_ids[:, 1:] — and with loss_mask[:, 1:].
DPO = -logsigmoid(beta * ((pi_chosen - ref_chosen) - (pi_rejected - ref_rejected))), averaged over the batch.

problems.title: Implement PPO for RLHF
problems.description: Build Proximal Policy Optimization with clipped surrogate objective, value function baseline, and KL penalty for RLHF.
problems.question: v3/alignment-training/ppo-rlhf/ppo-rlhf.ipynb
hints: generate_sequences starts from a BOS token (id = vocab_size), samples one token at a time from Categorical(logits=logits[:, -1, :]), and returns the running input ids so the value model can be scored on the same prefixes.
GAE runs backwards: delta_t = r_t + gamma*V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t) with V(s_T)=0, then A_t = delta_t + gamma*lam*A_{t+1}.

ppo_step recomputes log-probs for `actions` under the current policy, forms ratio = exp(new - old), and takes min(ratio*A, clamp(ratio, 1-eps, 1+eps)*A). total_loss = -policy_objective + 0.5*value_loss + kl_beta*kl_div.

For kl_div use the k3 estimator exp(ref - new) - (ref - new) - 1, averaged over tokens. mean(new - ref) has the right value but zero expected gradient, so as a loss term it never pulls the policy back toward the reference.

problems.title: Implement Gradient Checkpointing
problems.description: Trade compute for memory by recomputing intermediate activations during backward instead of storing them all.
problems.question: v3/alignment-training/gradient-checkpointing/gradient-checkpointing.ipynb
hints: In forward: stash fn on ctx, ctx.save_for_backward(*args), and run fn(*args) inside torch.no_grad() so no intermediate activation is kept.

In backward: detach the saved inputs, requires_grad_ them, re-run fn inside torch.enable_grad(), then torch.autograd.backward(outputs, grad_outputs) — unlike autograd.grad on the inputs, that also reaches fn's own parameters.
backward must return one gradient per forward argument — None for fn itself, then a gradient (or None) for each tensor input (read them off the detached copies).

Autograd only calls backward if some tensor argument requires grad. When none does (plain input data), have checkpoint() pass an extra dummy tensor with requires_grad=True, or the wrapped layer's weights never train.

Dropout inside fn: save torch.get_rng_state() in forward, and in backward restore it inside torch.random.fork_rng() before recomputing, so the replay draws the same mask without disturbing the RNG stream of the rest of training.

problems.title: Implement Mixture of Experts Layer
problems.description: Build a sparse MoE layer with top-k routing, gate-weighted combination of expert outputs, and a Switch-style load-balancing loss.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/mixture-of-experts/mixture-of-experts.ipynb
hints: Route each token to its top-k experts and weight their outputs by the gate probabilities.

Renormalize the top-k gate values so each token's weights sum to 1 (a softmax over just the k selected logits). Dispatch per expert: find the (token, slot) pairs that chose it, run only those tokens, and index_add the weighted outputs back.

Switch-Transformer aux loss: num_experts * sum_i f_i * P_i, where f_i is the fraction of routing assignments sent to expert i (a count, no gradient) and P_i is the mean softmax router probability of expert i (this carries the gradient). Uniform routing gives 1.

problems.title: Implement Speculative Decoding
problems.description: Draft tokens with a fast model, verify in parallel with the target model, and accept/reject to guarantee identical output distribution.
problems.question: v3/llm-inference/speculative-decoding/speculative-decoding.ipynb
hints: Draft phase: sample K tokens from the draft one at a time, keeping the draft probability q(x_i) of each. Verification: ONE target forward over prompt + all K drafts gives every p(x_i) at once.

Accept token i with probability min(1, p(x_i)/q(x_i)). On rejection, stop and sample the replacement from the normalised residual max(0, p - q) — that correction is what keeps the output distribution exactly the target's.
The target logits that score draft token i live at position prompt_len - 1 + i. If all K are accepted you get a free bonus token from position prompt_len + K - 1.

problems.title: Implement Continuous Batching for LLM Inference
problems.description: Dynamically slot sequences in and out of a running batch as they finish, maximizing throughput without padding waste.
problems.question: v3/llm-inference/continuous-batching/continuous-batching.ipynb
hints: Keep two lists: waiting_queue and active_batch. Each step() fills free slots from the queue first, then runs the model, then evicts whatever finished.
A request is done when it emits eos_token_id OR len(generated_ids) reaches max_gen_len — check both after appending the token.
step() should report whether work remains (active or waiting), so run() can simply loop `while self.step(model): pass`.

Batch the forward pass: right-pad every active sequence to the longest with eos_token_id, call the model ONCE on (num_active, max_len), and read row i's logits at its own last real position, length_i - 1. A causal model never looks at pads that come after a sequence.

problems.title: Implement DDPM from Scratch
problems.description: Build the full denoising diffusion pipeline: forward noise schedule, U-Net denoiser, and reverse sampling to generate images.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/ddpm/ddpm.ipynb
hints: linear_beta_schedule is torch.linspace(beta_start, beta_end, timesteps) — small betas first, so early steps corrupt slowly.
q_sample is the closed form of the forward process: x_t = sqrt(abar_t)*x_0 + sqrt(1-abar_t)*noise, with abar gathered per sample from t (each row of the batch has its own timestep).

p_sample: mu = (1/sqrt(alpha_t)) * (x_t - beta_t/sqrt(1-abar_t) * eps_pred), then add sqrt(beta_t)*z for t > 0 and nothing at t = 0. p_sample_loop starts at x_T ~ N(0, I) and calls p_sample for t = T-1 ... 0.

problems.title: Implement DDIM Sampling + Classifier-Free Guidance
problems.description: Build deterministic DDIM sampling with classifier-free guidance to control image generation quality and conditioning adherence.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/ddim-cfg/ddim-cfg.ipynb
hints: The null/unconditional label is the extra embedding row at index num_classes, so the class embedding table needs num_classes + 1 entries.
CFG: eps = eps_uncond + guidance_scale * (eps_cond - eps_uncond). At guidance_scale = 1 that is exactly eps_cond.

DDIM (eta=0): x0_pred = (x_t - sqrt(1-abar_t)*eps) / sqrt(abar_t), then x_prev = sqrt(abar_prev)*x0_pred + sqrt(1-abar_prev)*eps. No randn anywhere in the step — the only randomness is the initial x_T.

problems.title: Implement Selective State Space Model (Mamba)
problems.description: Build Mamba's selective scan mechanism with input-dependent parameters, achieving linear-time sequence modeling without attention.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/mamba/mamba.ipynb
hints: Discretize first: A_bar = exp(delta[..., None] * A) and B_bar = delta[..., None] * B[:, :, None, :], both (B, L, D, N).
Then run the recurrence over time with h of shape (B, D, N): h = A_bar[:, t] * h + B_bar[:, t] * x[:, t, :, None], y_t = (h * C[:, t, None, :]).sum(-1).
Two things are easy to lose: the skip connection y = y + D * x, and causality in MambaBlock — Conv1d(padding=d_conv-1) must be truncated back to L so no position sees the future.

problems.title: Implement Vision Transformer + MAE Pretraining
problems.description: Build ViT with masked autoencoder pretraining — randomly mask patches, encode visible ones, decode to reconstruct.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/vit-mae/vit-mae.ipynb
hints: PatchEmbedding is a Conv2d with kernel_size = stride = patch_size, then flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) to get (B, n_patches, embed_dim).
ViT: prepend a learned [CLS] token, add a positional embedding of length n_patches + 1, run the encoder, and return either the CLS row or every token.

MAE: shuffle patch indices with argsort(rand), keep the first int(N*(1-mask_ratio)), encode only those, re-insert mask tokens, unshuffle with ids_restore, and average the squared error over MASKED patches only -- (per_patch_mse * mask).sum() / mask.sum().

problems.title: Write a Fused Softmax Kernel in Triton
problems.description: Write a GPU kernel in Triton that fuses the softmax computation into a single pass, eliminating intermediate memory reads.
problems.question: v3/gpu-systems/triton-fused-softmax/triton-fused-softmax.ipynb
hints: Online softmax keeps a running max and running sum in one pass.
When a new max arrives, rescale the accumulated sum by exp(old_max - new_max).
Subtracting the running max before exp() is what keeps it stable on large inputs.

problems.title: Implement FlashAttention-2 in Triton
problems.description: Write the tiled, fused attention kernel that computes exact attention in O(n) memory using online softmax in Triton.
problems.question: v3/gpu-systems/flash-attention-triton/flash-attention-triton.ipynb
hints: Outer loop over Q blocks, inner loop over K,V blocks; the only matrix you ever materialize is the (block_q, block_kv) tile of scores.

Carry running_max, running_sum and running_output per Q block. When a tile raises the max, rescale BOTH the running sum and the running output by exp(old_max - new_max) before adding the tile's contribution.
Normalize once, after the inner loop: output = running_output / running_sum. The last block may be short, so slice with min(start + block, N).

Causal: a K,V tile that starts after the Q tile's last row is pure future — skip it. Only tiles straddling the diagonal need a mask (-inf where key > query); the first tile always contains key 0, so no row is ever fully masked.

problems.title: Implement FSDP from Scratch
problems.description: Build Fully Sharded Data Parallel: shard parameters across GPUs, all-gather before forward, reduce-scatter gradients after backward.
problems.question: v3/gpu-systems/fsdp/fsdp.ipynb
hints: shard() is torch.chunk into world_size pieces (detached clones, since each rank owns its own memory); all_gather() is torch.cat of those pieces.
reduce_scatter is reduce THEN scatter: sum the per-rank full gradients elementwise first, then chunk the sum so rank i keeps chunk i.
forward_on_rank should all-gather the weight and bias shards, run F.linear(x, full_weight, full_bias), and drop the gathered copy afterwards — that release is what makes the memory saving real.

compute_gradient_shards is data parallelism: split x and grad_output into one micro-batch per rank, let each rank compute grad_out_r.T @ x_r, then reduce_scatter. Gathering the shards must give exactly grad_output.T @ x.

problems.title: Implement GRPO (DeepSeek-R1 Algorithm)
problems.description: Build Group Relative Policy Optimization that scores multiple completions per prompt and uses group-relative advantages.
problems.question: v3/alignment-training/grpo/grpo.ipynb
hints: Generation: repeat_interleave each prompt group_size times so one prompt's completions sit in a contiguous block, then sample token by token.
Advantages are normalised INSIDE each group: reshape rewards to (num_prompts, group_size), subtract the row mean, divide by the row std + eps. No value model, no global mean.
grpo_loss = -mean(min(ratio*A, clip(ratio, 1-eps, 1+eps)*A)) + beta*KL, with ratio = exp(policy_logps - old_logps) and A broadcast over the tokens of its sequence.

The KL is the paper's per-token estimator: with d = ref_logps - policy_logps, KL = exp(d) - d - 1, averaged over tokens. mean(policy_logps - ref_logps) can go negative and has zero expected gradient as a loss.

problems.title: Build a Complete LLM Inference Engine
problems.description: Combine KV caching, continuous batching, and memory management into a production-grade inference server.
problems.question: v3/llm-inference/inference-engine/inference-engine.ipynb
hints: The cache stores K and V as (B, heads, seq_len, d_head) and update() concatenates the new step along dim=2. In cached mode you only project the NEW token into q/k/v and attend over the whole cached K/V.
MiniTransformer has to know where it is: when a cache is passed, the positional embedding index for the incoming token is the cache's current seq_len, not 0.

top_p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches top_p: sort descending, cumsum, zero out the tail, RENORMALISE, sample, then map the sampled index back through sorted_indices.

Prompts of different lengths: LEFT-pad them so every row's last prompt token is in the last column, pass a (B, kv_len) padding mask so no query attends to a pad key (pads stay in the KV cache), and give each row its own position ids that count real tokens only.

problems.title: Implement Knowledge Distillation
problems.description: Train a smaller student model to match a larger teacher's soft predictions using temperature-scaled KL divergence loss.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/knowledge-distillation/knowledge-distillation.ipynb
hints: Two terms: a KL divergence between the temperature-softened teacher and student distributions, and ordinary cross-entropy against the hard labels; alpha blends them as alpha * soft + (1 - alpha) * hard.

The soft term is KL(teacher_T || student_T): F.kl_div takes the student's log_softmax(s / T) as its input and the teacher's softmax(t / T) as its target, with reduction='batchmean' ('mean' would also divide by the number of classes).
Multiply the soft term by T**2: its gradients scale like 1/T^2, so without the factor the soft targets fade as T grows. The hard-label cross-entropy uses the raw student logits (T = 1).

problems.title: Implement Ring Attention for Long Contexts
problems.description: Distribute attention computation across GPUs in a ring topology, enabling context lengths that exceed single-GPU memory.
problems.question: v3/gpu-systems/ring-attention/ring-attention.ipynb
hints: ring_step is FlashAttention's inner loop: new_max = max(running_max, S.max(-1)), correction = exp(running_max - new_max), then rescale BOTH the running sum and the running output by that correction before adding the block.
Divide by running_sum only once, at the very end — never inside the loop.

Causal masking is per chunk pair: skip a K,V chunk whose index is greater than the Q chunk's (all future), apply a triangular mask when the indices are equal, and mask nothing when the K,V chunk is in the past.

problems.title: Implement a Swin Transformer Block (Shifted Window Attention)
problems.description: Build a Swin Transformer block from scratch: window partition, shifted-window attention masks, and a learned relative position bias.
problems.question: v3/modern-architectures/swin-transformer/swin-transformer.ipynb
hints: window_partition: reshape (B, H, W, C) to (B, H/ws, ws, W/ws, ws, C), permute the two window axes next to each other, then flatten. window_reverse undoes exactly that permutation.

The shifted mask compares region labels: label each pre-shift position by which of the (up-to) 4 wrapped regions it belongs to, roll the label map the same way you roll the features, partition it, and allow a pair only when the two labels match.

The relative position bias is one learned scalar per relative offset: build a (w*w, w*w) index map from (row_i - row_j, col_i - col_j) shifted to be non-negative, gather the table with it, and ADD the result to the attention scores before the softmax.

problems.title: Decision Tree Classifier (CART)
problems.description: Build a CART classification tree from scratch with Gini splits found by a vectorized sort-and-cumsum search over every threshold.
problems.question: v4/ml-fundamentals/decision-tree/decision-tree.ipynb
hints: Grow the tree recursively: at each node try every feature and every candidate threshold, keep the split with the lowest weighted child Gini, and stop at max_depth, below min_samples_split, or when no split strictly lowers the impurity.

Sort one feature column once. A cut after sorted position i sends the first i+1 samples left, so the left class counts for every cut are a cumsum of the one-hot labels in sorted order, and the right counts are total minus left.

With counts c_L and c_R, n_L*Gini_L + n_R*Gini_R = n - (|c_L|^2/n_L + |c_R|^2/n_R). Mask cuts between equal values, take the argmax over (cut, feature), and use the midpoint of the two neighbouring sorted values as the threshold (x <= t goes left).

problems.title: Principal Component Analysis via SVD
problems.description: Implement PCA from the SVD of the centered data: orthonormal components, unbiased explained variances, projection and reconstruction.
problems.question: v4/ml-fundamentals/pca/pca.ipynb
hints: Center the data first: PCA finds directions of maximum variance around the mean, not around the origin.
Take the thin SVD of the centered data, Xc = U S V^T. The rows of V^T are the principal directions, already sorted by decreasing singular value.
The covariance is Xc^T Xc / (N - 1) = V diag(S^2 / (N - 1)) V^T, so the explained variances are S^2 / (N - 1). Project with (X - mean) @ components.T and reconstruct with Z @ components + mean.

problems.title: Gaussian Mixture Model with EM
problems.description: Fit a full-covariance Gaussian mixture with expectation-maximization, using a log-space E-step, closed-form M-step and a monotone likelihood history.
problems.question: v4/ml-fundamentals/gmm-em/gmm-em.ipynb
hints: Alternate two steps. E-step: responsibilities r[n, k] = p(component k | x_n). M-step: re-estimate weights, means and covariances as responsibility-weighted averages. Do the E-step in log space.

log r[n, k] = log pi_k + log N(x_n | mu_k, Sigma_k) - logsumexp over k of the same. For log N use a Cholesky factor: Sigma = L L^T, solve L z = x - mu, then log N = -0.5 * (D log 2pi + 2 sum log diag(L) + |z|^2).

With N_k = sum_n r[n, k]: pi_k = N_k / N, mu_k = sum_n r[n, k] x_n / N_k, Sigma_k = sum_n r[n, k] (x_n - mu_k)(x_n - mu_k)^T / N_k + reg_covar * I. Record the mean log-likelihood (the mean over n of the logsumexp) at init and after every M-step.

problems.title: Gradient Boosting Regressor
problems.description: Implement gradient-boosted regression trees for squared loss, including your own variance-reduction regression tree, shrinkage and staged predictions.
problems.question: v4/ml-fundamentals/gradient-boosting/gradient-boosting.ipynb
hints: Start from the constant that minimizes squared error, F_0 = mean(y). For squared loss the negative gradient at each point is just the residual y - F(x), so every stage fits a small regression tree to the current residuals.

Write a regression tree whose splits minimize SSE_left + SSE_right and whose leaves predict the mean target. After sorting a feature, SSE_L + SSE_R = sum(r^2) - (S_L^2/n_L + S_R^2/n_R), where S_L is a prefix sum (cumsum) of the sorted targets.

Update F <- F + learning_rate * tree(X) after each stage and predict F_0 + learning_rate * sum of all tree outputs. staged_predict yields that running sum after each tree; return a new tensor each time rather than mutating one in place.

problems.title: Box IoU and Non-Maximum Suppression
problems.description: Implement vectorized pairwise box IoU, greedy non-maximum suppression, and class-aware batched NMS from scratch.
problems.question: v4/vision/iou-nms/iou-nms.ipynb
hints: box_iou: give boxes1 a new axis so it is (N, 1, 4) and boxes2 (1, M, 4); elementwise max/min of the corners then broadcast to (N, M) with no loop. NMS itself is inherently sequential: sort by score and walk the list once.

Intersection width = (min of the right edges - max of the left edges), clamped at 0; same for height. Union = area1 + area2 - intersection, and it can be 0 for two zero-area boxes. In NMS only a box you KEEP may suppress others, and it suppresses when IoU > threshold (strictly).

nms: compute the full IoU matrix once, visit boxes in descending-score order, skip any already suppressed, otherwise keep it and mark everything with IoU above the threshold as suppressed. batched_nms: either run nms per label, or shift every box by label * (max - min + 1) so boxes of different labels can never overlap and call nms once.

problems.title: Object Detection mAP
problems.description: Compute all-point interpolated average precision and detection mAP@IoU with greedy score-ordered matching across images.
problems.question: v4/vision/detection-map/detection-map.ipynb
hints: Split it in two: (1) turn a ranked list of TP/FP flags into precision and recall arrays, (2) turn those arrays into one number. AP is the area under the precision-recall curve after replacing each precision by the best precision achievable at that recall or higher.

For AP: prepend recall 0 and append recall 1 with precision 0, take a reverse running max of precision (flip, cummax, flip), and sum (recall step) x (interpolated precision). For mAP: per class, sort ALL its predictions across images by score, keep a 'used' flag per GT, and only compare a prediction with GTs of the same class in the same image.

A prediction is a TP if, among the unmatched same-class GTs in its image, the one with the highest IoU has IoU >= threshold (mark it used); otherwise FP. Cumulative sums of the TP and FP flags give precision = TP / (TP + FP) and recall = TP / num_gt_of_class. Average AP only over classes that have at least one GT.

problems.title: Classification Metrics from Scratch
problems.description: Implement confusion matrix, macro/micro precision-recall-F1, tie-aware ROC-AUC, step-wise average precision and expected calibration error in vectorized PyTorch.
problems.question: v4/ml-fundamentals/classification-metrics/classification-metrics.ipynb
hints: Everything except ECE falls out of counting: a confusion matrix gives per-class TP/FP/FN, and for ranking metrics one sort of the scores gives every threshold at once. Encode each (true, pred) pair as a single integer so one counting op builds the whole matrix.

TP is the diagonal, FP the column sums minus the diagonal, FN the row sums minus the diagonal. For AUC, rank all scores (tied scores share their average rank); the rank-sum of the positives gives the Mann-Whitney U. For AP, sort descending, cumsum the labels, and evaluate precision and recall only at the LAST position of each run of equal scores.

AUC = (sum of positive ranks - n_pos(n_pos+1)/2) / (n_pos * n_neg). AP = sum over distinct thresholds of (recall step) x precision. ECE: bin index from the max probability with torch.bucketize on the interior edges (right-closed bins), then per-bin sums of correct and confidence via bincount with weights; ECE = sum_b |sum(correct) - sum(conf)| / N.

problems.title: MLP Backprop by Hand (No Autograd)
problems.description: Implement Linear, ReLU and a numerically stable softmax-cross-entropy with hand-written backward passes, and train an MLP with SGD — no autograd.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/mlp-backprop/mlp-backprop.ipynb
hints: Write the chain rule for one element first: y[n, o] = sum_i x[n, i] * W[o, i] + b[o], so dL/dW[o, i] = sum over the batch of dL/dy[n, o] * x[n, i]. Every gradient has exactly the shape of the thing it is the gradient of — use that to pick the matmul.

Linear.forward must cache its input. backward: grad_W = grad_out.T @ x  (out, in), grad_b = grad_out summed over the batch, grad_x = grad_out @ W. ReLU lets the gradient through only where the forward input was strictly > 0.

Softmax-CE: subtract each row's max before exp (log-sum-exp), loss = mean(logsumexp(z) - z[target]); its gradient w.r.t. the logits is (softmax(z) - onehot(target)) / N. MLP.backward walks self.layers in reverse; step() does W -= lr * grad_W, b -= lr * grad_b.

problems.title: Micrograd: A Scalar Autodiff Engine
problems.description: Build a scalar reverse-mode autodiff engine: operator overloading, accumulated gradients on shared nodes, and an iterative topological sort.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/micrograd/micrograd.ipynb
hints: Every operation returns a new Value that remembers its inputs plus a tiny closure `_backward` which, given out.grad, adds (local derivative x out.grad) into each input's .grad. Ask yourself why it must ADD rather than assign.

backward(): build a topological order of the graph (each node after all of its inputs), set self.grad = 1.0, then call _backward on the nodes in reverse order. Use an explicit stack instead of recursion so a chain 5000 nodes deep still works.

Derive most ops from a few primitives: a - b = a + (-b), a / b = a * b**-1, -a = a * -1. The reflected ops wrap the Python number with the operands in the right order (1 - v is Value(1) - v, 1 / v is Value(1) / v). Local derivatives: tanh' = 1 - tanh^2, sigmoid' = s(1 - s), exp' = exp, log' = 1/x, (x^k)' = k x^(k-1).

problems.title: Normalization Layers & Dropout from Scratch
problems.description: Implement BatchNorm2d (with running statistics), LayerNorm, GroupNorm and inverted Dropout as nn.Modules that match PyTorch's outputs and gradients in train and eval mode.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/normalization-layers/normalization-layers.ipynb
hints: All three norms compute (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) followed by a learnable per-feature affine; they differ only in WHICH axes the statistics are taken over. For an (N, C, H, W) input: BatchNorm over (N, H, W) for each channel, LayerNorm over the trailing normalized_shape dims of each sample, GroupNorm over (C/G, H, W) for each sample and group.

Normalize with the biased variance (unbiased=False). BatchNorm in training also updates running = (1 - momentum) * running + momentum * batch_stat under torch.no_grad(), using the UNBIASED variance (x n/(n-1), n = N*H*W) for running_var; in eval it normalizes with the running stats. Store them with register_buffer, and branch on self.training.

GroupNorm: reshape to (N, G, -1) so each group holds C/G consecutive channels, normalize over the last dim, reshape back, then apply weight/bias of shape (C,) viewed as (1, C, 1, 1). Dropout: draw a keep-mask with P(keep) = 1 - p, return x * mask / (1 - p) in training, x itself in eval, and zeros when p == 1 (dividing by 1 - p = 0 would give NaN).

problems.title: Training Utilities: SGD, Warmup + Cosine LR, Gradient Clipping, EMA
problems.description: Implement torch.optim.SGD (momentum, Nesterov, weight decay), a linear-warmup + cosine LR schedule, global-norm gradient clipping and a weight EMA that match PyTorch exactly.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/training-utilities/training-utilities.ipynb
hints: Write each update rule down before coding: what does PyTorch store in the momentum buffer, and is weight decay added before or after momentum? For the schedule, sketch lr(step) and mark warmup_steps and total_steps.

SGD: g = grad + wd*p; buf = g on the first step, else buf = mu*buf + g; the step direction is g + mu*buf for Nesterov, buf otherwise; skip params whose .grad is None. Clipping: ONE norm over all gradients together, sqrt(sum of squared entries).

model.parameters() is a one-shot generator: list() it if you iterate twice. Clip coefficient = max_norm / (total_norm + 1e-6), applied only when it is < 1; return the pre-clip norm. EMA: keep detached clones, update under torch.no_grad() with s.mul_(decay).add_(p, alpha=1 - decay), copy buffers as-is.

problems.title: Loss Functions from Scratch: Cross-Entropy, BCE, Focal and Dice
problems.description: Implement F.cross_entropy (class weights, ignore_index, label smoothing, K-dim inputs), stable BCE-with-logits with pos_weight, RetinaNet's sigmoid focal loss and soft Dice loss, matching PyTorch values and gradients.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/losses-from-scratch/losses-from-scratch.ipynb
hints: Work in log space. log_softmax(x) = x - logsumexp(x) never forms exp(large). For BCE, -log(sigmoid(x)) = softplus(-x) = log(1 + exp(-x)): compute it with torch.logaddexp(0, -x) or F.softplus(-x). Move the class axis last and flatten, so (N, C, d1, ...) becomes (M, C) with M targets.

Mean reduction is a WEIGHTED mean: divide by the sum of w[target] over non-ignored targets, not by N. Replace ignored targets by a valid index before gather(), then zero them out. PyTorch's label smoothing = (1-eps) * NLL + (eps/C) * sum_c w_c * (-log p_c), with both terms normalised by the same denominator.

BCE: loss = (1-y)*x + (1 + (pos_weight-1)*y) * softplus(-x). The hand-written max(-x,0) + log1p(exp(-|x|)) has the right value, but autograd gets the slope wrong at exactly x = 0. Focal: p_t = p*y + (1-p)*(1-y), loss = alpha_t * (1-p_t)^gamma * BCE with alpha_t = alpha*y + (1-alpha)*(1-y) (none when alpha < 0), averaged over ALL elements. Dice per sample: 1 - (2*sum(p*t) + eps) / (sum(p) + sum(t) + eps), then the batch mean.

problems.title: Debug a Broken Training Pipeline
problems.description: Find and fix 9 silent bugs (data layout, normalisation, model head, training and evaluation loops) in a small image-classification pipeline, reasoning from symptoms to causes.
problems.question: v4/dl-fundamentals/debug-training/debug-training.ipynb
hints: Debug from symptoms. Look at an image after every transform, print the per-channel mean/std of the normalised training set, and evaluate the same model twice. For each line of the training loop, ask which state it depends on and who resets that state.

Data side: reshape() never moves axes (only permute/transpose do), and that includes a reshape you use to group values by channel. Model side: what does nn.CrossEntropyLoss apply to its input itself? Loops: what puts a model into train/eval mode, what clears .grad, and what keeps an autograd graph alive?

There is one bug each in to_tensor, compute_normalization_stats and make_model, none in normalize, and three each in train_one_epoch (mode, gradient reset, loss bookkeeping) and evaluate (mode, autograd, how the predicted class is extracted).

problems.title: Bilinear Interpolation from Scratch
problems.description: Re-implement F.interpolate's bilinear (both align_corners conventions) and nearest resize as vectorized gathers, matching PyTorch values and gradients.
problems.question: v4/vision/bilinear-interpolation/bilinear-interpolation.ipynb
hints: Bilinear is separable: work out, for each output row, which two input rows it reads and with what weights, do the same for columns, then gather and blend. Those index/weight vectors depend only on the sizes, never on pixel values.

align_corners=False maps output index d to src = (d + 0.5) * in/out - 0.5 (pixel centres line up) and PyTorch clamps a negative src to 0; align_corners=True maps d to d * (in - 1)/(out - 1), and to 0 when out == 1.

From src: i0 = floor(src) clamped to in-1, i1 = min(i0 + 1, in-1), w = src - i0. Index whole rows with x[:, :, i0, :] and x[:, :, i1, :], blend with (1-w) and w reshaped to broadcast over the row axis, then repeat along the last axis.

problems.title: Mixup and CutMix Augmentation
problems.description: Implement batch-level Mixup and CutMix with soft labels, a recomputed CutMix lambda and all randomness drawn from a torch.Generator.
problems.question: v4/vision/mixup-cutmix/mixup-cutmix.ipynb
hints: Both functions pick one lam per batch and one random permutation perm of the batch; sample i is mixed with sample perm[i]. Labels are mixed with the same lam and perm, so a one-hot row becomes lam on its class and 1 - lam on the partner's.

torch.distributions.Beta cannot take a generator. A Beta(a, a) draw is G1 / (G1 + G2) with G1, G2 independent Gamma(a) draws, and torch._standard_gamma(concentration_tensor, generator=g) draws Gammas from your generator; torch.randperm and torch.randint take generator= too.

CutMix: cut_h = int(H * sqrt(1 - lam)), cut_w likewise, centre (cy, cx) uniform over the image, clip the box edges to [0, H] and [0, W], copy that region from x[perm] into a clone of x, then set lam = 1 - box_area / (H * W) before mixing labels.

problems.title: Time-Conditioned U-Net (Diffusion Denoiser)
problems.description: Build a small time-conditioned U-Net (sinusoidal timestep embedding, GroupNorm ResBlocks, concatenated skips) of the kind used as a diffusion denoiser.
problems.question: v4/vision/unet/unet.ipynb
hints: Build bottom-up: the embedding is a fixed function of t (no parameters), ResBlock is norm-act-conv twice with the projected time embedding added in between, and the UNet only wires ResBlocks, downsamples and upsamples together.

In ResBlock the time projection gives (N, out_ch); index it with [:, :, None, None] so it broadcasts over H and W. When in_ch != out_ch the residual needs a 1x1 conv so skip(x) + h has matching channels. Return the sum as is, nothing after it.

In UNet.forward keep a list: after each encoder level's ResBlock append h, then downsample (except at the last level). In the decoder walk the levels in reverse: torch.cat([h, skips.pop()], dim=1), a ResBlock whose in_ch is the sum of both widths, then upsample (except at the top level).

problems.title: Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and the ELBO
problems.description: Build a VAE with the reparameterization trick and the negative-ELBO loss (Bernoulli BCE-with-logits + analytic KL, beta-weighted) and train it on binary bar images.
problems.question: v4/generative/vae/vae.ipynb
hints: The encoder predicts logvar = log(sigma^2), not sigma, so the standard deviation is exp(0.5 * logvar). Sampling z = mu + sigma * eps with eps drawn separately keeps z a differentiable function of mu and logvar.

Reconstruction: F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, x, reduction='sum') divided by the batch size, so it is summed over pixels and averaged over samples. Use the same convention for the KL: sum over latent dims, mean over the batch.

KL(N(mu, sigma^2) || N(0, 1)) per latent dim is -0.5 * (1 + logvar - mu^2 - exp(logvar)); sum it over latent dims, average over the batch, then loss = recon + beta * kl. sample(n) decodes z = torch.randn(n, latent_dim) and applies a sigmoid.

problems.title: Flow Matching (Rectified Flow) with Euler Sampling
problems.description: Implement conditional flow matching with the linear (rectified-flow) path used by SD3/Flux: interpolation, velocity-regression loss and an Euler ODE sampler.
problems.question: v4/generative/flow-matching/flow-matching.ipynb
hints: Everything follows from one straight line per pair: x_t = (1 - t) * x0 + t * x1 moves from noise (t = 0) to data (t = 1) at constant speed, so its time derivative — the regression target — is x1 - x0, independent of t.

t has shape (N,) but x0 may be (N, D) or (N, C, H, W): reshape t to (N, 1, ..., 1) before mixing. When x0 / t are None, draw x0 with torch.randn_like(x1) and t with torch.rand(N) (one time per sample), then return the mean squared error between model(x_t, t) and x1 - x0.

Euler: dt = 1 / num_steps; for k in 0 .. num_steps-1, call the model at t = k * dt (a (N,) tensor filled with that value) and update x = x + dt * v. Do not update x0 in place and do not call the model at t = 1.

problems.title: Diffusion Transformer (DiT) Block with adaLN-Zero
problems.description: Build a Diffusion Transformer block with adaLN-Zero conditioning, a sinusoidal timestep embedder, and patchify/unpatchify for latent images.
problems.question: v4/generative/dit-block/dit-block.ipynb
hints: adaLN-Zero turns the conditioning vector c into six (B, D) vectors with one Linear(D, 6D) after a SiLU: a shift, scale and gate for the attention branch and for the MLP branch. Initialise that Linear's weight and bias to zero — every gate is then 0, so each residual branch contributes nothing and the block starts as the identity.

Shapes: x is (B, N, D) but shift/scale/gate are (B, D) — unsqueeze(1) so one vector applies to every token of its sample. modulate is x * (1 + scale) + shift (the 1 + keeps scale = 0 neutral). Each branch is x = x + gate * f(modulate(LayerNorm(x), shift, scale)) with a LayerNorm that has no affine parameters (adaLN supplies them).

Chunk order: shift_msa, scale_msa, gate_msa, shift_mlp, scale_mlp, gate_mlp = adaLN_modulation(c).chunk(6, dim=1). patchify: reshape (B, C, H/p, p, W/p, p), permute to (B, H/p, W/p, p, p, C), flatten to (B, H*W/p^2, p*p*C); unpatchify undoes exactly those steps in reverse.

problems.title: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) from Features
problems.description: Compute feature statistics and the Fréchet distance between two Gaussians — the FID math — stably in float64 via a symmetric eigendecomposition.
problems.question: v4/generative/fid/fid.ipynb
hints: FID fits a Gaussian to each feature set, so feature_statistics is just the mean and covariance of the rows. Use the unbiased covariance (divide by N - 1), the same convention as torch.cov(feats.T) and numpy.cov.

The only hard term is Tr((S1 S2)^{1/2}). S1 S2 is not symmetric, but it is similar to the symmetric PSD matrix S1^{1/2} S2 S1^{1/2}, so both have the same non-negative eigenvalues lambda_i and the trace is sum(sqrt(lambda_i)).

In float64: S1^{1/2} = V diag(sqrt(clamp(w, 0))) V^T from torch.linalg.eigh(S1); M = S1^{1/2} S2 S1^{1/2}; symmetrise M; then tr_covmean = eigvalsh(M).clamp(min=0).sqrt().sum() and FID = |mu1 - mu2|^2 + tr(S1) + tr(S2) - 2 * tr_covmean. Don't call eigvalsh on S1 @ S2 itself — it is not symmetric.

problems.title: SigLIP: Sigmoid Loss for Language–Image Pre-training
problems.description: Implement SigLIP's pairwise sigmoid image-text loss with a learnable temperature and bias, numerically stable and normalized by batch size as in the paper.
problems.question: v4/multimodal/siglip-loss/siglip-loss.ipynb
hints: There is no softmax over the batch: every (image i, text j) pair is its own binary classification. The N matching pairs on the diagonal are positives (z = +1); the other N^2 - N pairs are negatives (z = -1).
L2-normalize both embedding sets along the feature dim, then logits = exp(logit_scale) * img @ txt.T + logit_bias. Build the +/-1 label matrix from torch.eye (2*I - 1).

loss = -(sum of log-sigmoid(z * logits)) / N — divide by the batch size N, not by N^2, so it is not a .mean() over the matrix. Use F.logsigmoid: log(sigmoid(x)) underflows to -inf for very negative x. SigLIPHead stores logit_scale = log(10) and logit_bias = -10 as nn.Parameters.

problems.title: VLM Connector: MLP Projector, Perceiver Resampler and Image-Token Merging
problems.description: Build the pieces that connect a vision encoder to an LLM: a LLaVA-style MLP projector, a Flamingo-style Perceiver Resampler, and the vectorized merge of image features into the token sequence with LM labels.
problems.question: v4/multimodal/vlm-connector/vlm-connector.ipynb
hints: The projector is applied to every image token independently. The resampler turns a variable number of image tokens into a fixed number by letting num_queries learned vectors (an nn.Parameter) be the attention queries, with the image tokens as keys and values.

Resampler layer: LayerNorm the image tokens and the latents, q = W_q(latents), k/v from the image tokens (Flamingo also appends the latents to k/v), multi-head attention, residual add, then a pre-LN MLP with a second residual. Expand the latents over the batch dim; never add positions to the image tokens.

Merge: a (B, L) boolean mask of placeholder positions tells you everything. Check its per-row count equals T (else raise ValueError), then write the flattened (B*T, D) image features into a clone of text_embeds through that mask — boolean indexing visits positions in row-major order, which is exactly 'k-th feature of sample b -> k-th placeholder of sample b'. Labels = input_ids with placeholder and attention_mask == 0 positions replaced by ignore_index (no shift).

problems.title: Vector Search: Chunked Exact Top-k, an IVF Index and Recall@k
problems.description: Implement memory-bounded exact top-k search (cosine, dot, L2), an IVF approximate index with an inline k-means quantizer, and recall@k, as used for image-text retrieval and RAG.
problems.question: v4/multimodal/vector-search/vector-search.ipynb
hints: Exact search is one matrix multiply per database chunk: compute a (Q, chunk) score block, keep its best k, and merge that with the best k found so far (concatenate the two candidate sets and take top-k again). Remember to add the chunk's start offset to the indices.

cosine = dot product of L2-normalized vectors; l2 = ||q||^2 - 2 q.d + ||d||^2, clamped at 0, and you want the SMALLEST k (topk(largest=False)). A chunk can be smaller than k, so take min(k, chunk) there.

IVF: k-means (random initial centroids from the data, alternate assign / recompute the mean, keep a centroid whose cluster went empty) gives nlist centroids; add() appends each vector's global id to its nearest centroid's list; search() scores only the vectors in the nprobe nearest lists and pads with id -1 and the worst score. recall@k = |approx ∩ exact| / k averaged over queries (order does not matter, -1 never counts).

problems.title: Ring All-Reduce and DDP Gradient Averaging
problems.description: Simulate W ranks and implement the bandwidth-optimal ring all-reduce (reduce-scatter + all-gather) through a message-logging network, then use it to average gradients across model replicas like PyTorch DDP.
problems.question: v4/systems/ring-allreduce/ring-allreduce.ipynb
hints: Give every rank a private working copy split into W chunks with torch.tensor_split (sizes differ by at most one, empty chunks are fine). Phase 1 (reduce-scatter) leaves each rank owning one fully-summed chunk; phase 2 (all-gather) passes those finished chunks around the ring.

Reduce-scatter step s: every rank r first sends chunk (r - s) % W to rank (r + 1) % W, then every rank receives from rank (r - 1) % W and ADDS the message into chunk (r - 1 - s) % W. After W - 1 steps rank r owns the complete sum of chunk (r + 1) % W.

All-gather step s: rank r sends chunk (r + 1 - s) % W, receives into chunk (r - s) % W and OVERWRITES it (copy_, never +=). For DDP: torch.cat the trainable grads (zeros_like(p) where p.grad is None) into one flat vector per replica, all-reduce once, divide by W, then torch.split by p.numel() and view_as(p) to write the grads back.

problems.title: INT8 Quantization from Scratch
problems.description: Implement symmetric (per-tensor and per-channel) and asymmetric int8 quantization, dequantization, and an int8 linear layer with exact integer accumulation and a single float rescale.
problems.question: v4/systems/int8-quantization/int8-quantization.ipynb
hints: Symmetric: qmax = 2^(b-1) - 1 (127 for 8 bits) and the scale maps the largest |x| exactly onto qmax. Asymmetric: the 2^b - 1 steps span [min(x.min(), 0), max(x.max(), 0)] and the zero point is the integer code that represents 0.0.
